lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Welcome back! Today's tale reaches back some seventy million years, to the age of the <color=red>dinosaurs</color>.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Read it <color=red>attentively</color>, then answer four questions. Answer them all correctly and four new books will join the library's collection.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Dr Ines Okafor had spent a decade studying <color=red>fossilised</color> footprints, convinced that tracks could reveal more about dinosaurs than bones alone.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: In a dried riverbed she uncovered a remarkable <color=red>trackway</color>: dozens of large prints heading in one direction, with smaller prints sheltered in the centre.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Her colleagues assumed the herd had been fleeing a <color=red>predator</color>, but Ines noticed that the strides were short and evenly spaced, suggesting the animals had been walking calmly.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: She proposed that these dinosaurs travelled in protective family groups, a <color=red>hypothesis</color> that has since inspired a whole generation of researchers.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Question 1: What did Ines believe footprints could reveal?
choices: Exactly how old the Earth is
More about dinosaurs than bones alone
lines.hint: Not quite. Reread the first part of the story.
lines.correctText: Correct. She thought tracks could tell us more than bones alone.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Question 2: Why were the smaller prints in the centre significant?
choices: They showed smaller dinosaurs chasing larger ones
They had been made on a different day
They suggested young dinosaurs were being protected
lines.hint: Not quite. Notice the word sheltered, and think about her final conclusion.
lines.correctText: Yes. The herd seems to have surrounded its young.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Question 3: What evidence led Ines to doubt that the herd was fleeing?
choices: The strides were short and evenly spaced
There were no predator prints nearby
The riverbed was too deep to run through
lines.hint: Not quite. Look at what she noticed that her colleagues had missed.
lines.correctText: Exactly. Short, even strides suggest a calm walk, not a panicked run.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Question 4: In the final part, what does <color=red>hypothesis</color> most nearly mean?
choices: A proposed explanation that can be tested
A detailed map of a site
lines.hint: Not quite. She proposed the idea; it had not yet been proven.
lines.correctText: Well reasoned. A hypothesis is an idea put forward to be tested.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Impeccable reasoning. You'd make a fine <color=red>palaeontologist</color>. Four new books are on their way to the library.

afterLines.speaker: Tilly
afterLines.text: Thanks again. I hear the library's new arrivals include a superb <color=red>illustrated</color> guide to prehistoric life.
